items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, decision block and c1 together say what to do (beta, provisionally), why (65% right totals against gamma's 45%, both inside the $1.00-per-1,000 and 800 ms bars, alpha out on both at $4.00 and 1001 ms), and the main risk (the +20-point lead's corrected interval, -9.3 to +47.6, reaches zero, and gamma becomes the pick if it is noise). Watch adds the nearest line: turn time 99 ms under the bar, p95 791.6 ms.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: c1 (bars rule alpha out) leads to c2 (inside the bars beta leads gamma, unseparated), then c3 (what separating them takes, 240 against 60 trials) and c4 (every failure is a wrong total). Nothing contradicts the headline. One gap: the campaign kind says a pick shown ahead on no pair rests on cost or simplicity, or no clear winner is called. The report picks the costlier arm on a point estimate without saying it departs from that rule, though it does explain its departure on the bars (Method). The strongest support it has, a same-size rerun reading gamma ahead only 8.1% of the time, sits in Watch rather than in the recommendation.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: Beta's weak axes are visible: its lead is a point estimate in the headline, the recommendation and c2, turn time is its nearest line (701 ms mean, p95 791.6 ms against 800 ms), and gamma is cheaper and faster. Alpha's unseparated lead over beta (-7.1 to +39.3) is stated, not hidden. Confidence is low with every caveat open.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Most omissions check out: the unpaired beta-gamma interval (-0.08 to +0.48) does not separate, the unpaired alpha-beta interval does just clear zero (+0.0007) but alpha is out on the bars, production cost equals measured spend for every arm, the frozen failures carry no reply or expected total, and price_tradeoff's $1.50 is per whole unit of the rate. But the first omitted item misstates code's dominance. Code has gamma dominating beta and beta dominating alpha. Gamma does not dominate alpha, which is ahead of it on answers, separated (+4.6 to +74.2). The stated reason ('reads the bars as warnings') also misses the material part: gamma's dominance over beta holds inside the bars too, so code's own reading of the very pair the pick rests on favours gamma.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: All 17 snapshot caveats appear with a material_if clause. best_of_n, no_control and nothing_declared carry into the lede, the decision and next steps 1 and 2. ingest_backlog is singled out in next step 3, and its clause names the right risk: a backlog difference would move turn time and answer rate together, which is the very pattern that separates gamma (faster, fewer right totals) from beta. The other apparatus caveats share a 'record it on every run' step. The orchestration_ms gap is explained as not bearing on the bar.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names an experiment or a declaration and what it settles: a larger paired rerun of beta and gamma, a minimum answer rate, recording the apparatus settings, and a case-by-case failure comparison. Two weak spots. Step 1 says 240 trials without saying they must be fresh cases at today's three repeats (settle counts trials, but the intervals are over cases, so 240 trials on today's 20 cases would not separate the arms). Step 4's logic, that different failing cases point to noise, is loose.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: c1's bars with budget lines and c4's per-arm check table fit their claims, and the counterfactual holds for both. c2's dot_interval shows each arm's own interval, not the corrected pair interval the claim cites (-9.3 to +47.6). If the own intervals overlapped while the pair interval separated, the block would not change, and the caption only says so. c3's block is a scoreboard of trials run, passed and failed, plus reply and test cost. It shows the 60, but nothing about what separating the arms takes: the 240 figure and the 8.1% wrong-side rate never reach a block.

findings.finding: Omitted item 1 misdescribes code's dominance. options_dominance has gamma dominating beta and beta dominating alpha. Gamma does not dominate alpha, which is ahead of it on answers, separated (+4.6 to +74.2). The reason given (bars read as warnings) also misses that gamma's dominance over beta holds inside the bars, so the pipeline's reading of the pair the pick rests on favours gamma. Restate it correctly, and either move it out of Omitted into the gamma why_not or say why answering outranks code's cost tie-break.

The campaign kind says a pick shown ahead on no pair rests on cost or simplicity, at low confidence, or no clear winner is called. Beta is shown ahead on no pair, yet it is picked over the cheaper gamma. Say this departs from the kind's rule and why, and move the strongest reason into the recommendation: a run of today's size reads gamma ahead only {settle.beta.gamma.goal_state:reply.total == case.total.overall.wrong_side|pct} of the time. Today that figure sits only in Watch.

The scoreboard block shows trials run, passed and failed, plus reply and test cost (the cost cells print unlabelled raw dollars, such as 0.0008). It does not show the claim's own figure, 240 trials to separate the arms, or the 8.1% wrong-side rate. Use a block that shows the settle sizing against today's 60, or drop the block and let c3 rest on c2.

The claim rests on the corrected pair interval (-9.3 to +47.6 at 98%), but the dot_interval shows each arm's own 95% interval. Show the pair difference with its corrected interval, or say in the claim text that the block shows the arms' own spreads.

In what_settles_it, next step 1 and c3, the 240 is trials (settle counts trials on a repeated design), while Method says the intervals are over cases. Say it is fresh cases at today's {repeats|int} repeats each. Otherwise a reader could add repeats to today's 20 cases and not separate the arms.

The minimum-answer-rate control reads a floor on the point estimates (between 45% and 65% leaves beta alone). The report reads the bars on the whole interval, and beta's own interval (0.44 to 0.82) would not clear a floor of 50% read that way. Say which reading the floor uses.

The turn-time control says a bar inside or below beta's interval leaves gamma the only arm inside. That is wrong below gamma's own interval (373.3 to 428.7 ms), where no arm qualifies. Bound the statement.

invariant_concerns: Invariant 1: three numbers are typed in prose, not read through a figure key: 'the nine frozen failures' (Omitted), 'corrected across the three pairs' (c2 caption and Method), and 'a hundred points' (Omitted).

Invariant 5: the c4 evidence table's column headers print measure keys (reply.cites_policy, reply.total == case.total), and the c3 scoreboard prints 'reply cost usd' and 'test cost usd' as row labels, all above the appendix. This may be the renderer's doing rather than the document's.
Invariant 6: Method is present. The report-doc has no full-results appendix field to check, so this could not be verified from the document.
